_comment:
What is now believed, on what evidence, and what would overturn it.

A run record says what happened. A graph card says which arm won. NOTHING in MLClaw said what is now BELIEVED — and that is the only thing anybody repeats six weeks later, out loud, with none of the three qualifiers that made it true. Borrowed from ARA (arXiv:2604.24658) `logic/claims.md`, whose shape is the contribution: `Evidence basis` and `Interpretation` are SEPARATE COLUMNS, and a claim without `Falsification criteria` is not admitted.

What is MLClaw's and not ARA's: a conclusion here can go `unverifiable`. ARA's statuses assume the evidence stays put; MLClaw retires datasets, deletes checkpoints and loses snapshots, so `supported` and `refuted` do not cover the case that actually happens — the corpus was retired and NOBODY CAN CHECK ANY MORE. That is not a weak `supported`. It is the same three-way split as `census.py` (`gone` vs `unreachable`) and `/repro`'s four verdicts, one level up.

‼️ `status` and `tier` are COMPUTED, never written. `conclude.py check` derives them from what the evidence currently resolves to, and reports where the stored value disagrees. Hand-editing them is the whole failure this file exists to prevent: a conclusion whose confidence outlived its evidence.
_comment_conclusions:
One entry per belief. Fields:

  id             K01, K02… Never reused, never renumbered — a conclusion is cited by id from run records, chat, and other conclusions.

  statement      What is now believed, in one sentence. ! Every NUMBER in it must appear in an `evidence[].quote` — `check` matches digits, same rule as `graph.py`'s number grounding. Write the belief, not the argument for it.

  scope          {corpus, mode, metric}. A conclusion is about a CORPUS, not about the world. `datasets/boxes@260731` and `datasets/boxes@260812` are different scopes and a conclusion does not carry across. This is CLAUDE.md's "Never let a share measured somewhere else stand for this corpus" at the belief level, and it is the field that makes "we tried it, it did not help" answerable six weeks later.

  evidence       [{kind, ref, quote, tier}]. `ref` must RESOLVE — `check` opens it. `quote` is the transcribed line, not a summary: a bare path is not grounding. `tier` is the tier THAT NUMBER was measured at, and it travels forever (CLAUDE.md).

  interpretation What is argued ON TOP of the evidence and was not measured. ARA's own example keeps "the authors argue (but do not formally prove)" in this field and out of the statement. Separating them is the entire borrowing: fused, a conclusion reads as if the mechanism were measured, and the next round designs against a mechanism nobody tested.

  falsified_if   REQUIRED. What measurement would overturn this. Must name a number or a metric — "if it turns out not to work" is a tautology and passes everything. A belief with no falsifier is not a conclusion; it is a preference, and `check` refuses it.

  depends_on     Other conclusion ids this rests on. Refuting a dependency does NOT delete its dependents — it CONTESTS them, and somebody has to look. See `_comment_status`.

  provenance     user | ai-suggested | ai-executed | user-revised. Never auto-upgrades.
_comment_status:
COMPUTED by `check`, five states, and the middle one is the one ARA does not have:

  supported     every `evidence[].ref` resolves and reads as recorded; no dependency is weaker.
  contested     something recorded disagrees — an open dispute, a later measurement, or a contested/refuted dependency. TWO RECORDS MAY DISAGREE WITHOUT ONE BEING ERASED; this state is where they sit until somebody rules.
  refuted       `falsified_if` was met by a recorded measurement. Set only by `refute`, which requires the ref that did it.
  unverifiable  ‼️ an evidence ref no longer resolves — run deleted, snapshot retired, node gone. The conclusion is NOT false and must never be reported as refuted, and it must never be left at `supported` either. Somebody could check yesterday and cannot today; that is a third fact.
  superseded    replaced by a sharper conclusion. Requires a resolvable `superseded_by`; the old one is kept, because what was believed at the time is what explains the runs launched at the time.
_comment_tier:
COMPUTED: the WEAKEST tier among `evidence[]`, by T0 < T1 < T2 < T3. Not the strongest, not the one you would like. A conclusion resting on one T3 arm and one T1 probe is a T1 conclusion, and quoting it later as controlled is exactly how a false noise floor entered a record once already (CLAUDE.md).

T4 is not on that ladder — it is an approximation priced for the original, so it cannot carry a conclusion ABOUT the original. `check` flags it rather than ranking it.
